agree.reason: The page reads as honest and likeable, but an owner whose cousin does her books for $600 a year sees $2,388 and gets no reason to change or to tell her cousin, so she probably won't book.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief and the $800 claim is hedged, but the promise to warn clients before the 10th and the line that they'll get 'a finished, reconciled year' are commitments the brief never states.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $2,388 a year, which is the least flattering form of the price, but it never says that nobody left by choice (29 of 31 stayed, and the 2 who left sold their salons), that 9 of 12 closes were on time, or how the $800 saving compares with the extra cost.

right_comparison.reason: It never describes her real alternative, which is a once-a-year catch-up by her cousin while she handles payroll and sales tax herself all year, so the reader has nothing to set $199 a month against.

qualification.reason: The deadline hedge is a good one: it names the 10th, admits three misses and says what happens if one is coming, but the tax-time saving is hedged with nothing the reader can check.

objections.reason: Her main objection, paying about four times what her cousin charges and leaving him, goes unanswered, for example by saying he can keep doing her taxes from cleaner books, while space goes on the price rise, which she never asked about.

fit.reason: It is about 330 words of page copy with clear sections and ends with the button to book the call, as the brief asked.
